alignments.note: Hithpael takes subject, auxiliary and lexical verb; the reflexive myself renders the verb's own voice and stays in its unit (rules 17, 44).
Hithpael with its reflexive pronoun; the subject and auxiliary are not rewritten for this coordinated clause.
Niphal takes subject, auxiliary and the make ... known rendering with its reflexive, headed on the lexeme-bearing known (rules 17, 44).
Construct noun with no article morpheme in the chain takes the supplied the (rule 29).
Verb takes subject, auxiliary and lexical verb (rule 17).
Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own I (rule 20).
The predicate of the verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula (rule 20).

review_notes: The three reflexive pronouns are kept with their verbs, since Hithpael and Niphal voice licenses them (rule 44's reflexive rider) rather than their being supplied objects.
In the closing recognition formula the copula goes to the predicate Jehovah and only I to the explicit pronoun, per rule 20.
